title: Checks for ternary if expressions that can be replaced with the or operator.
summary: Ternary if expressions are more verbose than or expressions while providing the same functionality. Ruff takes this rule from refurb and made it stable in 0.15.0.

title: Checks for consecutive calls to append.
summary: Consecutive calls to append can be less efficient than batching them into a single extend. Each append resizes the list individually, whereas an extend can resize the list once for all elements. Ruff takes this rule from refurb. It is in preview.

title: Checks for uses of bin(...)2: (or hex, or oct) to convert an integer into a string.
summary: When converting an integer to a baseless binary, hexadecimal, or octal string, using f-strings is more concise and readable than using the bin, hex, or oct functions followed by a slice. Ruff takes this rule from refurb and made it stable in 0.13.0.

title: Checks for lambda expressions and function definitions that can be replaced with a function from the operator module.
summary: The operator module provides functions that implement the same functionality as the corresponding operators. For example, operator.add is often equivalent to lambda x, y: x + y. Using the functions from the operator module is more concise and communicates the intent of the code more clearly. Ruff takes this rule from refurb. It is in preview.

title: Checks for the use of IOBase.write in a for loop.

title: Checks for uses of readlines() when iterating over a file line-by-line.

title: Checks for uses of set.remove that can be replaced with set.discard.

title: Checks for literals that are similar to constants in math module.

title: Checks for consecutive global (or nonlocal) statements.
summary: The global and nonlocal keywords accepts multiple comma-separated names. Instead of using multiple global (or nonlocal) statements for separate variables, you can use a single statement to declare multiple variables at once. Ruff takes this rule from refurb. It is in preview.

title: Checks for uses of hardcoded charsets, which are defined in Python string module.
summary: Usage of named charsets from the standard library is more readable and less error-prone. Ruff takes this rule from refurb. It is in preview.

title: Checks for unnecessary string literal or float casts in Decimal constructors.
summary: The Decimal constructor accepts a variety of arguments, including integers, floats, and strings. However, it's not necessary to cast integer literals to strings when passing them to the Decimal. Ruff takes this rule from refurb and made it stable in 0.12.0.

title: Checks for uses of bin(...).count("1") to perform a population count.

title: Checks for datetime.fromisoformat() calls where the only argument is an inline replacement of Z with a zero offset timezone.

title: Checks for math.log calls with a redundant base.

title: Checks for unnecessary from_float and from_decimal usages to construct Decimal and Fraction instances.
